result.topic_en: Gauss sets up a theory of astronomical refraction: he defines pressure, density and refractive index of air as functions of height, writes the refraction as an integral, and evaluates it by his quadrature formula, followed by numerical logarithmic computations.
result.transcription:
202
Theorie der Refraction.
$e$ Expansivkraft der Luft
$r$ Distanz vom Mittelpunkt der Erde
$c$ Dichtigkeit der Luft ; $m$ Brechungsverhältniss
$\frac{R}{r} = 1-s$
Es sei
$e = \mathcal{E}(1-\frac{s}{g})$
$m = \frac{1}{\sqrt{[1+\frac{c}{C}(\frac{1}{MM}-1)]}}$
$-\frac{dce}{ds} = \frac{R\mathcal{E}c}{l}$
$-\frac{de}{ds} - \frac{edc}{cds} = \frac{R\mathcal{E}}{l}$
Also
$\frac{edc}{cds} = -\frac{de}{ds} - \frac{R\mathcal{E}}{l} = \frac{\mathcal{E}}{g} - \frac{R\mathcal{E}}{l}$
$\frac{dc}{c} = \frac{ds}{1-\frac{s}{g}}(\frac{1}{g}-\frac{R}{l})$ ; also $g\frac{R}{l}-1=\lambda$ gesetzt
$\frac{(\lambda+1)l}{R} = g$
$c = C(1-\frac{s}{g})^{\lambda}$
$\mathcal{J}$ scheinbare Zenithdistanz ; $1-MM=\mu$
Refraction
$-\int \frac{\mu dx}{2(1-\mu x)} \cdot \frac{\sin \mathcal{J}}{\sqrt{(\frac{1-\mu x}{[1-g(1-x)^{\frac{1}{\lambda}}]^2} - \sin \mathcal{J}^2)}}$
8.4056202
2.934690
Meine Quadraturcoefficienten durch $k$ bezeichnet
$\frac{k\mu y}{1-\mu yy} = a$ $\frac{1-\mu yy}{(1-g(1-yy)^{\frac{1}{\lambda}})^2} = b$ $\frac{a}{\sqrt{b}} = A$ $\sqrt{\frac{b-1}{b}} = \mathfrak{B}$
$A = a\sqrt{(1-\mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{B})}$
Refraction $= \Sigma \frac{A \operatorname{tg} \mathcal{J}}{\sqrt{(1+\mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{B}\operatorname{tg}\mathcal{J}^2)}}$
[-$\mathfrak{B} = \sqrt{2g(1-yy)^{\frac{1}{\lambda}} - \mu yy}$-]
$\mathfrak{B} = \sqrt{\frac{2g[1-(1-yy)^{\frac{1}{\lambda}}] - \mu yy - gg[1-(1-yy)^{\frac{1}{\lambda}}]^2}{1-\mu yy}}$
$\mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{B} = 0.002465624\,yy + 0.001232975\,y^4 = 0.00246..yy(1+\frac{1}{2}yy)$

methods.what: Pressure assumed to decrease linearly with height variable s
Refractive index as function of air density
Resulting density law as a power of (1-s/g)
Refraction expressed as an integral over x
Evaluation of the refraction integral by Gaussian quadrature with coefficients k
Series approximation of B squared in y
